item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence (AI), with its groundbreaking advancements, has demonstrated its effectiveness and great impact on society.

The Institute for AI Innovation and Societal Impact (AI4LIFE) at Hanoi University of Science and Technology, in collaboration with the Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth Union and the Center for Student Innovation and Entrepreneurship, has established the “AI Young Talent Academy – AIYT”. Its mission is to support talented high schoolers in maximizing their potential and becoming future talents in the field of AI.

AIYT aims to be a hub for passionate and capable students with an inclination towards pursuing AI. Students participating in AIYT will benefit from:

  • Guidance and mentorship from leading Vietnamese researchers and experts in the field of AI.
  • Collaboration with talented university students who are studying and conducting research in AI.

 

Eligibility: High school students across the nation

Selection process:

Round 1: Application submission 
• Deadline: January 10, 2024, to January 31, 2024
• Apply via the link: https://forms.gle/TrZxLLQWZj5yZgpW7

Round 2: Mathematics and programming skills test

Round 3: Interview

item.content:encoded:
Professor Sushil Varma at University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, is currently seeking highly motivated PhD students to join his research group.

Professor Sushil Varma’s research focuses on:

  • Theoretical machine learning 
  • Reinforcement learning 
  • Queuing theory 

 

Application Details

  • How to Apply: Submit your application to the IOE Ph.D. Program.
  • Deadline: December 10, 2024.
  • Additional Step: Interested candidates are welcome to email the Professor directly at sushilv@umich.edu.

 

About Professor Sushil Varma

He is currently a Postdoctoral Fellow at INRIA Paris. He received my PhD from ISyE, Georgia Tech, and my B.Tech from the Mechanical Engineering Department at IIT Bombay. His work has been recognized through awards at IFIP Performance and INFORMS, and his thesis received the ACM SIGMETRICS Best Dissertation Award 2024.

 

For more information: Please visit his site

The post HUST-UTS Collaborative PhD Program appeared first on AI4LIFE.
item.content:encoded:
Eligibility

  • Bachelor’s/Master’s degree graduates with distinction or higher (CPA of 3.2 or above).
  • Proficiency in English (equivalent to IELTS 6.0 or above).
  • Passion for scientific research.
  • Prior experience in research projects and published papers is an advantage (but not mandatory).

 

Scholarship Programs

1. 89-Topup Scholarship

  • Designed for faculty members from universities.
  • Applicants will receive guidance on applying for the 89 Scholarship from the Ministry of Education, selecting UTS as their host university.
  • Upon receiving the 89 Scholarship, applicants will also receive a UTS top-up scholarship worth AUD 38,000/year and an additional AUD 5,000 start-up grant.

2. JRC Scholarship

  • For those ineligible for the Ministry of Education’s 89 Scholarship.
  • Recipients of the JRC Scholarship will study 1-2 years at HUST and at least 1 year at UTS.
  • While at HUST, they will receive funding from AI4LIFE Institute’s budget.
  • During their time at UTS, they will receive a full scholarship funded by UTS.

 

Selection Process

Round 1: Application Submission

  • Copy of Bachelor’s/Master’s degree (for Master’s graduates).
  • Academic transcripts from the most recent degree level.
  • Recommendation letters (at least two).
  • Acceptance letters from supervisors (one from HUST, one from UTS) (optional).

Submission link

Round 2: Interview

  • Presentation of research content and proposal.
  • Q&A with the selection committee.

 

Supervisors

  1. Supervisors at UTS: List 
  2. Supervisors at HUST

    • All faculty members at HUST (meeting HUST’s requirements for PhD supervision) are eligible to supervise candidates under this program.

    • Applicants may also refer to faculty members currently conducting research at AI4LIFE (here).

item.content:encoded:
On November 1, 2024, the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) and Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST) signed an agreement to establish a AIHub named Joint Research Center (JRC) at AI4LIFE Institute.

The AIHub was established to promote collaboration in applied AI research between the two universities. Through AIHub, UTS will annually fund four PhD scholarships for Vietnamese students, along with several top-up scholarships for faculty members who have received Scholarship 89 from the Vietnamese Ministry of Education.

Students participating in AIHub’s scholarship program will be co-supervised by researchers at both UTS and HUST.

After the signing ceremony, the senior leadership delegation from UTS visited and held a working session at HUST. During the session, the two sides discussed and outlined several plans for implementing dual-degree programs for bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD programs. The area of interest include Applied Artificial Intelligence and Semiconductor Technology.
